ios.desc:
Rate.fm (formerly Wavelength) is the “rate your music” app for iPhone — a fast, modern way to rate songs, write album reviews, and discover new music through real people.

Rate tracks and albums on a simple 10-point scale, write full reviews or quick reactions, and follow friends to see what they’re listening to. Build a personal music diary over time, track your listening history, and shape a taste profile that actually reflects you.

If you’ve been looking for a RYM-style community on mobile (or an AOTY-style way to browse what’s trending), Rate.fm delivers the same people-first discovery — Letterboxd-style, but for music.

MUSIC REVIEWS & RATINGS
• Rate songs and albums with a quick 10-point rating system
• Write detailed music reviews or short reactions
• Browse top songs, albums, and artists by community rating

SOCIAL MUSIC DISCOVERY
• Follow friends and see ratings, reviews, and listens in your feed
• Like, comment, and share music reviews
• Explore trending music based on community activity, not opaque algorithms

MUSIC DIARY & LISTENING STATS
• Log what you listen to and watch your taste evolve
• Build a music taste profile from your ratings and activity
• View user profiles with ratings, reviews, and listening history

SEARCH & BROWSE
• Search songs, albums, artists, and people
• Find reviews fast and discover your next favorite

Discover music. Review music. Follow your friends.

Terms of Use: https://rate.fm/terms
Privacy Policy: https://unionst.com/wavelength/privacy

show_hn.title: Show HN: Rate.fm – Letterboxd for Music, on iPhone and the Web

quotes.text:
I made rate.fm because every “Letterboxd for music” app sucked. I tried RYM (still 2004), AOTY (a charts website), and Musicboard (dying). I just wanted a fast diary where I could log what I heard, give it a number, write a little, and see what friends thought.

The app lets you rate albums and songs out of 10, write reviews, make lists, and follow friends. We aggregate scores from 19 publications (Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, NME, AllMusic, The Guardian) and show them on the pages as well. Connect Apple Music, Spotify, or Last.fm to log passively and get stats. You can rate whatever song is playing from the Lock Screen without opening the app, and import your Musicboard history with a tap.

Tech: UIKit and SwiftUI, Node on Vercel, Postgres on RDS. The catalog is about 226k albums and 563k songs, mostly from Apple Music, with MusicBrainz for the more obscure releases.

The hardest problem was a clean music library. Music identity is extremely convoluted: the same recording shows up across ISRCs, reissues, and regional storefronts, and basically every feature was broken until I folded them into one identity.

Free, no ads, iPhone only for now: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/rate-fm-rate-your-music/id6756295934

I’d love feedback on the onboarding, and whether you think the critic scores are a good feature or just a distraction.
